entries.title: fetch a released seed and let every tool take a stage1 compiler
entries.body:
A fresh clone or agent session can now fetch the last released compiler with one command. Every tool that ran the TypeScript compiler through `dist/index.js` can be pointed at a native stage1 binary instead. Every default is unchanged. This is the first step of retiring stage0 (docs/wp19-stage0-retirement.md, R6).

- `scripts/fetch-seed.sh` unpacks the last release into `build/seed/` through `install.sh`, so the download, the version check and the swap live in one place. It does nothing once a working seed is there. It also takes a version or `--force`.
- `tests/fetch_seed.js` checks the script against a stand-in installer, with no network. It has 13 checks, and each branch was watched failing.
- `tests/self/seed.js` looks in `build/seed/bin/nish` before falling back to stage0.
- The Claude Code on the web session hook fetches the seed without blocking the session. The project settings allow `build/nish`, the fetched seed, and the fetch script.
- `scripts/smoke.sh` and `docs/cookbook/regen.sh` take `NISH=<compiler>`, through the shared helper `scripts/nish-compiler.sh`. `bench/*.mjs` and `tests/nish/run.ts` take `--compiler <nish>`.
- `tests/nish/cli.ts` checks whether the compiler has the simulated-internal-error hook, instead of assuming only stage0 has it.
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: compile every golden with stage1 and stop comparing against stage0
entries.body:
The test suite and CI no longer need the TypeScript compiler.

A released seed builds the self-hosted compiler once per run. That one binary compiles every golden case, and the parallel case runner cut `npm test` from about 15 minutes to about 4. The checks that compared the two compilers are gone. Their successors are `nish-cmp`, which checks the last release against HEAD, and the recorded goldens. The guards that read the TypeScript compiler's internals now read the self-hosted compiler: the runtime table against `nish.h`, the allocating builtins, the seed targets and the exit-70 path. This is the second step of retiring stage0 (docs/wp19-stage0-retirement.md, R6).

The self-hosted compiler now keeps four command-line promises that only the TypeScript compiler used to keep:

- The usage text names the command `nish`. It used to say `compile`.
- `--link` checks for the C compiler it will use (`CC`, else `clang`) before compiling anything. If the compiler is missing, it exits 3 with an install hint for each platform, and under `--json` it prints one NL0002 object. No IR is left behind.
- Under `--json`, an internal compiler error is one NL0003 object on stdout, as the machine-readable contract requires.
- `NISH_SIMULATE_ICE=1` exercises the real exit-70 path for tests.

The 89 parser refusals whose wording differed now expect the self-hosted compiler's sentence, and `dump_ast` expects its tree. CI's `batch-parity`, `parity-select` and `parity-changed` jobs and the nightly `parity.yml` are removed.
metrics: npm test 2104 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped in 4m01s (main: 15m15s); nish-cmp 514/514 programs agree against the 0.6.0 seed
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: take the surviving test tools off stage0
entries.body:
Every test tool that outlives the TypeScript compiler now runs on a released seed or on a compiler it is given. The answers only that compiler could give are recorded before it is deleted. This is the third step of retiring stage0 (docs/wp19-stage0-retirement.md, R6).

- `tests/self/goldens/support.txt` records stage0's 340 answers: string escaping, float hex, package export targets and bare-specifier parsing. `support_oracle.js` checks against that file, so nothing is dropped when `dist/` is gone.
- The diagnostic-code registry `self/codes.ts` is now kept by hand. `scripts/gen-diagnostic-codes.mjs --check` validates it:
  - codes are well-formed and in their bands;
  - no code or fragment is used twice;
  - fragments are ordered, and none is under 10 characters;
  - `RULE_COUNT` matches.

  With no flags, the script prints the next free code in each band.
- The differential suite runs on frozen rewrites and a named compiler only. A new register, `tests/differential/goldens/unfrozen.txt`, names any program without a frozen rewrite instead of skipping it silently. Fuzzing against Node, which needed the TypeScript rewriter, is gone. Fuzzing the seed against HEAD remains.
- The 80 codes only stage0 could provoke are folded into `tests/wordings/unreachable.txt` as retired codes, each with its reason. The 41 parser-refused wording cases now pin the self-hosted parser's own sentence.
- The lexer, parser and support oracles, `nish-cmp`, `diagnostic_coverage.js` and `scripts/arrow-verify.mjs` no longer fall back to stage0.
metrics: npm test 2104 passed, 0 failed, 2 skipped; support 981/981 lines with dist/ removed; diagnostic coverage 265/411 codes, 146 unreachable with reasons, uncoded=5
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.breakingNote: the package no longer contains the TypeScript compiler (`dist/`), and `typescript` is no longer installed as a runtime dependency. Building from source needs a released `nish` seed (`scripts/fetch-seed.sh`) and clang.
entries.title: delete stage0, the TypeScript compiler
entries.body:
Nish now has one compiler: the self-hosted one in `self/`. The TypeScript implementation in `src/`, which was the bootstrap seed and the second implementation the oracles compared against, is deleted. This completes the retirement of stage0 (docs/wp19-stage0-retirement.md, R6).

- **Deleted.** Deleted along with `src/`: the six oracles that compared the two compilers (types, diagnostics, symbols, checked, IR, interop), `parity.js`, the stage1-only register, the differential rewriter and arrow-parity, and the `ddc` provenance job with `.github/ddc-tag.sh`. `ddc-0.6.0` is the last provenance tag taken while a second implementation existed.
- **What replaced each oracle.** `nish-cmp` compares the last release with HEAD, byte for byte, over the whole corpus. `tests/self/goldens/` records what the other four oracles compared. The golden cases compile with the self-hosted compiler.
- **Package.** `typescript` is no longer a runtime dependency; it stays a dev dependency for the lexer and parser oracles, the packaging checks, the codemod and `tsc` over the ambient declarations. The npm package ships 35 files, with no `src/`, no `dist/` and nothing that imports `typescript`. There is no Node compiler inside it: on a platform without a prebuilt binary, the launcher refuses (already true since 0.6.0).
- **Scripts.**
  - `npm run build` builds `build/nish` with the released seed that `scripts/fetch-seed.sh` downloads.
  - `npm run check` is now `tsc --noEmit` over `self/`, `std/` and `tests/nish/` against `runtime/nish.d.ts`. It holds the one documented divergence (`pop`) with a `@ts-expect-error` and fails if that line's error ever goes away.
  - `npm test` is `node tests/run.js`.
- **Releases.** Release binaries are built from the previous release's seed, and `scripts/bootstrap.sh --verify` still asserts `IR(stage1) == IR(stage2)` and a byte-identical `stage3 == stage2`.
metrics: npm test 2106 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (WASI) with NISH_BOOTSTRAP=0.6.0, 5m40s, nish-cmp green; npm pack 35 files; -33365 lines
entries.author: Amrit Kahlon

entries.title: describe one compiler in the rules and the live documents
entries.body:
* docs: describe one compiler in the rules and the live documents

WP19 R6 deletes `src/`, the TypeScript compiler that seeded and checked
`self/`. The rules and the live reference documents now describe the tree the
deletion leaves: one compiler, `self/`, built by the last released `nish`.

- `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/*.md`: a construct is implemented
  once, in `self/`, under the rolling freeze. `npm run check` is an ambient
  `tsc --noEmit` over `self/`, `std/` and `tests/nish/`. The seed comes from
  `scripts/fetch-seed.sh`. `self/codes.ts` is the hand-kept code registry,
  and the stage1-only register is gone.
- `README.md` and `docs/{ARCHITECTURE,MASTER_PLAN,INSTALL,LANGUAGE,IR_COOKBOOK,wp10-ci,wp12-release}.md`
  point at `self/` modules rather than `src/` ones, and describe CI and the
  release without the parity, batch and ddc jobs. The two Markdown links into
  `src/` now point into `self/`.
- `docs/wp19-stage0-retirement.md` and MASTER_PLAN's M6 mark R6 done. They
  record what the deletion removed and what replaced each oracle, and leave a
  placeholder for the dated measurement.
- Comments in `bin/`, `scripts/`, `runtime/` and `examples/` stop pointing
  at `src/` and `dist/`.

Refs: docs/wp19-stage0-retirement.md#5-order
Part of #144

* docs: correct the one-compiler rewrite where review found it wrong

Name only identifiers self/ defines, say the R6 gate is the 0.6.0 seed,
fetch the seed in every build-from-source recipe, point a nish-cmp
difference at its DECLARED list, and mark wp12's pre-R6 decision records
as superseded.

* docs: tighten the one-compiler rules after review

Point the definition of done at CLAUDE.md instead of restating it, say that
npm test builds its own compiler and runs the fixed point, give the
one-case golden update, and drop two references to rules and oracles the
rewrite removed.

* docs(self): state the seed order tests/self/seed.js actually uses

build/nish comes before the fetched release in build/seed/, as the merged
seed plumbing resolves it.

* docs: name self/ice.ts as the home of the NISH_SIMULATE_ICE hook

The harness stage put the hook beside the report it drives.
